meta.title: FROTH-RFC-0007: Triangulated Web Search via Multi-Provider Fan-Out
meta.author: Charlie (@charliebuddybot)

section.title: Problem
section.p: No single LLM provider has complete or unbiased web search.

Grok has x_search (native access to X's index) and web_search. OpenAI has browsing and search grounding. Gemini has Google Search grounding with inline citations. Anthropic has no native web search at all. Each provider's search has a different index, different freshness window, different political bias in result ranking, and different hallucination profile when results are sparse.

An agent with access to one provider's search sees the web through one eye. An agent with simultaneous access to three providers' search sees the web through three eyes. The value is not redundancy. It is triangulation. When three independent indexes agree, the fact is probably a fact. When they disagree, the disagreement is the most important part of the answer.

Today Charlie has no web search at all. Lennart has x_search and web_search via Grok's native tools. The xpost analyzer now uses grok_search. But none of these can cross-reference. None of them can say "Grok says X, Gemini says Y, and GPT says Z." The triangulation is manual — a human posts a link, Lennart searches it, Charlie comments on the search, and the human does the cross-referencing in their head.

section.title: Proposal
section.p: A single tool — web_search — available to any Froth agent, that fans out a search query to multiple LLM providers simultaneously, collects their responses, and returns a collated result.

subsection.title: The Fan-Out
subsection.code: web_search("Lindsey Graham Kharg Island Iwo Jima") | +---> Grok 4.20 (x_search + web_search) ---> response_grok +---> GPT 5.4 (browsing + search) ---> response_openai +---> Gemini 3.1 Pro (Google Search grounding) ---> response_gemini | v collation | v structured result returned to calling agent
subsection.p: All three calls happen concurrently via Task.async_stream or equivalent. The wall-clock cost is the slowest provider, not the sum. Typical: 2-5 seconds.

subsection.title: The Query
subsection.p: Each provider receives the same prompt:
subsection.code:
Search the web for: {query}
Return: 1. Direct factual findings with source URLs 2. Dates and timestamps where available 3. Explicit uncertainty markers where results are thin 4. If this is about a social media post, include the full text of the post
subsection.p: The prompt is adapted per provider to use their native search mechanism:

item.p: Grok: Uses the Responses API with x_search and web_search tools enabled. The model decides which to invoke.
OpenAI: Uses the Responses API with web_search_preview tool enabled.
Gemini: Uses google_search_retrieval grounding with dynamic retrieval threshold 0.3 (aggressive grounding).

The agent does not choose which providers to query. The agent does not see the individual provider responses. The agent sees one collated answer. The triangulation is infrastructure, not interface.

section.title: Relation to RFC-0002
section.p: RFC-0002 proposes a native multimodal LLM layer where each provider speaks its own API through adapters beneath a shared semantic core. This RFC depends on that architecture: Froth.Search.Grok, Froth.Search.OpenAI, and Froth.Search.Gemini each need native provider access to invoke vendor-specific search tools that do not exist in compatibility-mode endpoints.

item.p: Grok's x_search is only available through the Responses API.
OpenAI's web_search_preview is only available through the Responses API.
Gemini's google_search_retrieval is only available through the native Gemini API.

section.p: None of these exist in OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoints. The search RFC is the first consumer that makes RFC-0002's native provider layer load-bearing rather than aesthetic.

section.title: Cost Model

item.p: 3 provider calls (one per search engine): ~$0.01-0.05 each depending on model and response length
1 collation call (Sonnet): ~$0.005
Total: ~$0.02-0.16 per search

section.p: This is cheap enough to be a default tool on every agent. The expensive part is not the search. The expensive part is the agent cycle that calls the search, which already costs $0.50-2.00 in context tokens. Adding $0.10 of search to a $1.00 cycle is a 10% increase for a qualitative transformation in factual grounding.

item.p: One provider times out: Collation proceeds with two sources. The result notes which provider failed.
Two providers time out: Collation proceeds with one source. The result is explicitly marked as single-source, unverified.
All providers time out: Tool returns an error. The agent can retry or proceed without search.
Providers disagree: This is a feature, not a failure. The collation step presents the disagreement explicitly. The calling agent decides what to do with contradictory information.

Provider hallucinates despite search: Cross-referencing reduces this. If Grok hallucinates a fact that neither GPT nor Gemini found, the collation step flags it as single-source. The hallucination rate of the collated output is the product of the individual hallucination rates, not the sum. Three 5% hallucination rates produce a 0.0125% collated hallucination rate for facts that require two-source confirmation.
Build Froth.Search with the three provider modules.
Wire it as a tool in Froth.Agent.Config under the name web_search.
Add it to Charlie's tool list. Charlie gets web search.
Add it to any agent's tool list as needed.
Lennart keeps his native Grok x_search for speed — the triangulated search is for situations where accuracy matters more than latency.

section.title: What This Enables

item.p: Charlie can fact-check his own claims in real time.
Any agent can answer "what happened today" with citations.
The xpost analyzer could use triangulated search instead of single-provider Grok for high-stakes posts.
The hourly podcast can include verified news summaries.
The family stops depending on one provider's view of reality.

section.p: The tool is a prism. One beam of light goes in. Three beams come out. The colors that appear in all three beams are white. The colors that appear in only one beam are the beam's opinion. The difference between white and opinion is the entire value proposition of the tool.

section.title: Implementation Status
section.p: This RFC was implemented on 2026-03-24 and became obsolete on 2026-04-17.

def.desc: Implemented. Froth.Search.Grok uses native x_search and web_search through Froth's xAI Responses integration.
Implemented. Froth.OpenAI now auto-switches to Froth.LLM.Providers.OpenAIResponses when web_search_preview is present, so search runs through OpenAI's native Responses API path.
Implemented. Froth.Search.Gemini uses native google_search_retrieval grounding, and the provider/tool encoding is covered by tests.
Implemented. Froth.Search collates provider outputs into a structured Froth.Search.Result, and web_search is exposed through Froth.Inference.Tools for agent use.

section.p: Commit f1eccf1 removed Froth.Search, Froth.Search.Result, and the triangulated web_search tool. Current Froth uses explicit agent delegation and provider-native search capabilities instead of this bespoke fan-out and collation subsystem.
The API specification below is retained as historical documentation and is not available in the current codebase.

subsection.title: The Target Interface
Provider Calls
subsection.p: Each provider call follows the same pattern: send the query with web search tools enabled, collect the streaming response, extract text and citations.
subsection.code:
# Grok — works today, uses Froth.Grok directly Froth.Grok.stream_single( [%{"role" => "user", "content" => query}], on_event, tools: [%{"type" => "web_search"}, %{"type" => "x_search"}], model: "grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning", system: "Search the web. Return factual findings with source URLs." )
# OpenAI — implemented via Froth.OpenAI auto-switching to OpenAIResponses Froth.OpenAI.stream_single( [%{"role" => "user", "content" => query}], on_event, tools: [%{"type" => "web_search_preview"}], model: "gpt-5.4", system: "Search the web. Return factual findings with source URLs." )
# Gemini — implemented via native google_search_retrieval grounding Froth.Gemini.stream_single( [%{"role" => "user", "content" => query}], on_event, tools: [%{ "google_search_retrieval" => %{ "dynamic_retrieval_config" => %{ "mode" => "MODE_DYNAMIC", "dynamic_threshold" => 0.3 } } }], model: "gemini-3.1-pro", system: "Search the web. Return factual findings with source URLs." )

item.p: Froth.LLM.Providers.OpenAIResponses was added and wired into Froth.OpenAI for web_search_preview.
Froth.Search was implemented as the concurrent fan-out and collation coordinator.
web_search is exported through Froth.Inference.Tools for agent use.
Tests cover provider tool encoding, multi-provider fan-out, collation, and tool execution.
